title: feat!: explain the notation in the legend, tighten document checks and implement modeler-api 1.2
commits:
feat(schema-model)!: refuse ids that name built-in object properties

parseDocument accepted ids such as constructor, toString or __proto__,
but the canvas keeps its elements in a plain object, where these names
already resolve, so the import of such a file failed. documentIdProblems
now refuses every own property name of Object.prototype, as the Value
Chain schema model does, at the id's JSON path (e.g. flows.0.id), so the
renderer's importDocument and the VS Code Problems view refuse them too.
The plugin's checker mirrors the rule, and the conformance kit gets a
document with the id constructor as invalid text.

BREAKING CHANGE: parseDocument and documentIdProblems refuse ids that
name a built-in property of JavaScript objects (constructor, toString,
__proto__, hasOwnProperty, valueOf, ...).

Refs #128

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(schema-model): report issues at the file's index after migration drops interactions

When migrate() dropped a legacy interaction (one without position or
size), parseDocument reported the issues of later interactions at their
index in the migrated document, so the VS Code Problems view and every
other editor pointed at the wrong interaction. The migration now keeps
the file's index of every interaction it keeps, and parseDocument
reports schema issues and id problems under interactions at that index.

Refs #128

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): explain the notation next to its symbols in the legend

The notation primer left the help dialog in 0.11. It now lives in the
legend card of the web app and the VS Code webview: every team type,
interaction mode and other element gets one short line under its name
(what it stands for), and each group's heading says what its shapes
share: "Teams: solid, long-lived", "Interactions: dashed, short-lived".

Per the design system's legend (guide 5.10) the rows keep the 24px
preview and 13px text; the explanation and the group headings take the
muted text role, and the text column stays 200px wide, so every line
fits on one row and the card stays narrow next to the diagram. The
lists keep their names (Team types, Interaction modes, Other elements)
for screen readers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(renderer): keep an open label editor and its text across a view change

The label editor committed on canvas.viewbox.changing, and the
collaborative modeler's setViewState and every fit change the viewbox.
So a host that set its view or fitted the diagram while the user typed
committed the half-typed label: a change event, a new undo step and an
export with text the user had not confirmed (law L5 of the modeler-api
contract 1.2).

A view change now never commits. The editor stays open with what was
typed and is laid over its element again on canvas.viewbox.changed, in
the new position and at the new zoom. Only the user's own gestures end
an edit: Enter, Escape, a click or drag on the canvas (a pan starts with
one) and leaving the field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(renderer): implement the modeler-api contract 1.2

The renderer pins @miragon/modeler-api 1.2.0, so meta.apiVersion is
1.2.0, and implements what the contract adds:

- elements.bounds(id) gives a team's, interaction's, flow's or
  annotation's box in diagram coordinates, read from the live canvas,
  and undefined for every other id (connectors, roots, unknown ids),
  so hosts draw presence outlines and todo markers without reaching
  into the engine.
- The factory options take the contract's names: freeArea, as
  { insets } (px from the container's edges, the centre computed the
  way a fit does) or { center } (diagram coordinates), next to
  fitOnImport and undoRedoKeys, which already had these names.
  freeRectCenter stays accepted as the deprecated name of
  freeArea: { center } for one more minor release; given both,
  freeArea wins. Modeler and createCollaborativeViewer take the same
  options; the viewer ignores freeArea and undoRedoKeys. Both apps
  pass freeArea now.
- The conformance harness wires the new hooks: moveElement moves
  team_checkout through modeling.moveElements, commitInteraction
  presses Enter in the open label editor. All 26 cases of the 1.2 kit
  run and pass, without skips or advisories, the new L5 view-change
  case and the bounds case included.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names modeler-api 1.2.0; the lockfile also
catches up with the workspace versions of the last releases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: hand the focus back to the canvas after a click on chrome

Both apps and the private ui package pin @miragon/modeler-shell 0.2.2
(e2e too). After a pointer click on the zoom panel, a palette entry or
an action of the File and Model menu groups, the shell now hands the
keyboard focus to the canvas through the diagram-js viewport's focus(),
so Delete, the arrow keys and Cmd/Ctrl+Z act at once; Enter and Space
leave the focus on the control. Before, the focus stayed on the clicked
button and the next Delete went nowhere.

The shell's conformance kit adds the case focusHandBack, which runs in
both e2e projects (webapp and vscode-webview) and passes there.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names modeler-shell 0.2.2.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(schema-model)!: refuse an interaction without position or size from version 2 on

migrate() dropped every interaction without position and size, in any
document version, not only the edge-interactions of a version 1 file.
So a version 2 or 3 file whose interaction had lost its size opened
without a word, the VS Code Problems view stayed empty, and the next
edit saved the file without that interaction.

Only a version 1 file loses its edge-interactions now. From version 2
on, an interaction without geometry is refused at its path
(interactions.N.size) like any other missing field, so the renderer's
importDocument and the Problems view report it. The plugin's checker,
which already called it an error, now reports it at the missing field
for these versions and keeps "drops it on open" for version 1.

BREAKING CHANGE: parseDocument refuses a version 2 or 3 document with
an interaction that has no position or size instead of dropping that
interaction.

Refs #128

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
